nodes.label: Flora Plugin Contract (meta + build)
nodes.rationale: A drop-in plugin file exports exactly two things: `meta` ({id, label, category}) and `build(seed) -> THREE.Object3D` whose base sits at y=0. Zero-registration: dropping the file in the folder makes the prop placeable in both the World Editor and the live game on startup. Seed-driven variation is conventional (not required) so scattered patches don't look identical.

nodes.label: Plugin Props Are Always Walk-Through
nodes.rationale: Two prop registration paths exist deliberately. The lightweight plugin path has no collider and is always walk-through, like built-in flowers/grass/ferns. The hand-registered catalog (propTypes.js + props.js, e.g. tree-birch, flower-snowdrop) exists precisely because those props need real collision — a tree you cannot walk through. Anything needing a solid collider (big rock, structure) must use the manual path instead.

nodes.label: Duplicate meta.id Silently Overwrites
nodes.rationale: A plugin whose meta.id collides with a built-in prop or another plugin silently overwrites the earlier registration — last one loaded wins, with no error. meta.id is also the value persisted into world.json, so a collision corrupts placed-prop identity.

nodes.label: check:props Does Not Scan the Plugin Folder
nodes.rationale: `npm run check:props` validates only the hand-authored catalog, so plugin files get no automated validation at all. The prescribed substitute is manual: place it in the World Editor and eyeball it — does it stand on the ground, does it hold up across a few different seeds.
nodes.norm_label: check:props does not scan the plugin folder

nodes.label: Plugin category Must Match an Existing Palette Tab
nodes.rationale: meta.category must be one of trees | plants | rocks | decor, as defined by PROP_CATEGORIES in src/sim/propTypes.js. The plugin system deliberately cannot add new palette tabs.
nodes.norm_label: plugin category must match an existing palette tab
